## Assignment

Carry out the analysis as outlined in ISLR2 Chapter 3 Lab (**3.6.1 through 3.6.5**); however, instead of using base R plotting, perform all graphical analysis using ggplot2.

### Interpretation (required)

In 2–4 sentences, state what your model says about the relationship in plain language — the kind of sentence you'd say to a colleague who won't read your code. Then note one diagnostic or assumption that gives you pause, and why.


## 3.6.1 Libraries

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
# library(MASS)
library(ISLR2)
library(broom)
library(car)
library(patchwork)
```

## Data

I recommend that you not "attach" the data to the project as shown in the 

```{r}
Boston
```

## 3.6.2 Simple Linear Regression

```{r}
boston_fit <- lm(medv ~ lstat, data = Boston)

summary(boston_fit)
```

## Structure of model output

We didn't cover this in class, but you can see what is in the `boston_fit` object using the `str` function.

```{r}
str(boston_fit)
```


### Names (can be seen in the above output)

```{r}
names(boston_fit)
```


###  Coefficients 

```{r}
coef(boston_fit)
```


### Confidence Interval

```{r}
confint(boston_fit)
```


### Prediction interivals 

```{r}
predict(boston_fit, tibble(lstat = c(5, 10, 15)), interval = "confidence")
```

```{r}
predict(boston_fit, tibble(lstat = c(5, 10, 15)), interval = "predict")
```

### Base R plot (try to avoid)

```{r}
plot(Boston$lstat, Boston$medv)
abline(boston_fit)
```

Following along in the book; for information (exploration) only.

```{r}
plot(Boston$lstat , Boston$medv , col = "red")
plot(Boston$lstat , Boston$medv , pch = 20)
plot(Boston$lstat , Boston$medv , pch = "+")
plot(1:20 , 1:20 , pch = 1:20)
```

When passing a model object to the `plot()` funcdtion, get several charts; however, I find only the first two to be readily accessable and they can be reproduced in `ggplot()` with data generated using the `augment()` function from `broom`.

```{r}
plot(boston_fit)
```

```{r}
plot(predict(boston_fit), residuals(boston_fit))
plot(predict(boston_fit), rstudent(boston_fit))
```

```{r}
plot(hatvalues(boston_fit))
which.max(hatvalues(boston_fit))
```


## Create a ggplot of the main plot, medv vs lsat

The `augment()` function from the broom package creates a data frame with all the information needed to reproduce the plot above.

```{r}
augment(boston_fit) |> 
  ggplot() +
  geom_point(aes(lstat, medv), shape = 21) +
  geom_line(aes(lstat, .fitted))
```

### Residuals versus fitted values

```{r}
augment(boston_fit) |> 
  ggplot() +
  geom_point(aes(.resid, .fitted), shape = 21)
```

### Leverage: residuals vs .hat

```{r}
boston_aug <- augment(boston_fit) |> 
  mutate(observation = row_number())

boston_aug |> 
  ggplot(aes(.hat, .resid)) +
  geom_point(shape = 21) +
  geom_text(
    data = boston_aug |> filter(.hat == max(.hat)),
    aes(label = observation),
    position = position_nudge(y = 2)
  )
```

### Histogram of residuals

```{r}
augment(boston_fit) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = .resid)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50)
```

### Quantile-quantile plot

```{r}
augment(boston_fit) |>
  ggplot(aes(sample = .resid)) +
  geom_qq() +
  geom_qq_line()
```

## 3.6.3 Multiple Linear Regression

```{r}
boston_fit_v2 <- lm(medv ~ lstat + age, data = Boston)

summary(boston_fit_v2)
```

```{r}
boston_fit_v3 <- lm(medv ~ ., data = Boston)

summary(boston_fit_v3)
```

```{r}
vif(boston_fit_v3)
```

## 3.6.4 Interaction Terms

```{r}
boston_fit_v4 <- lm(medv ~ lstat*age, data = Boston)

summary(boston_fit_v4)
```

## 3.6.5 Non-linear Transformations of the Predictors

```{r}
boston_fit_v5 <- lm(medv ~ lstat + I(lstat^2), data = Boston)

summary(boston_fit_v5)
```

>We use the anova() function to further anova() quantify the extent to which the quadratic fit is superior to the linear fit.

```{r}
anova(boston_fit, boston_fit_v5)
```

An R plot of the model

```{r}
plot(boston_fit_v5)
```

### ggplot of the predicted values versus actual values and residuals 

```{r}
p1 <- augment(boston_fit_v5) |> 
  ggplot() +
  geom_point(aes(medv, .fitted))

p2 <- augment(boston_fit_v5) |> 
  ggplot(aes(medv, .resid)) +
  geom_point()

p1 / p2 +
  plot_layout(heights = c(4, 2), axes = "collect")
```


```{r}
augment(boston_fit_v5) |> 
  ggplot(aes(medv, lstat)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = "y ~ x + I(x^2)")
```
